title: System Design Interview Framework: Quick Revision
summary: A night-before revision of the step-by-step system design interview framework: clarifying requirements, back-of-envelope estimation, API and data model, high-level design, deep dives, trade-offs and common mistakes.

chapters.title: The Framework and Clarifying Requirements
points: Framework order: requirements → estimates → API → data model → high-level design → deep dives → bottlenecks/trade-offs; drive it yourself and state the plan up front
Functional requirements = what the system does (post tweet, follow user); pick the 2-3 core features and explicitly put the rest out of scope
Non-functional requirements = how well: availability vs consistency (CAP choice), latency target (e.g. p99 < 200 ms), scale, durability, security
Ask scale questions first: DAU, read/write ratio, data size per item, geographic spread, growth in 1-5 years
Write requirements on the board and get the interviewer to confirm them before designing; assumptions stated out loud are never wrong

layout.note: Step flow from requirements to trade-offs
Interview Point: 2-4 questions on scoping and NFRs

chapters.title: Back-of-Envelope Estimation
points: QPS = DAU × actions per user per day ÷ 86,400 (≈10^5 s/day); peak QPS ≈ 2-3× average
Example: 100M DAU × 10 reads/day = 10^9 ÷ 10^5 ≈ 10,000 read QPS; at 10:1 read/write ratio ≈ 1,000 write QPS
Storage = writes per day × size per item × retention; e.g. 1M posts/day × 1 KB × 365 × 5 yr ≈ 1.8 TB; add ×3 for replication
Bandwidth = QPS × payload size; e.g. 10,000 QPS × 100 KB = 1 GB/s egress, which drives CDN need
Round aggressively to powers of 10 and show the arithmetic; the goal is order of magnitude, not precision

layout.note: Worked estimate for a 100M DAU service

chapters.title: Numbers Every Engineer Should Know
points: Powers of two: 2^10 = 1 KB (~thousand), 2^20 = 1 MB (~million), 2^30 = 1 GB (~billion), 2^40 = 1 TB, 2^50 = 1 PB
Latency ladder: L1 cache ~1 ns, main memory ~100 ns, SSD random read ~100 µs, same-datacenter round trip ~0.5 ms, HDD seek ~10 ms, cross-continent round trip ~150 ms
Memory is ~1000× faster than SSD and SSD ~100× faster than HDD seek; avoid disk seeks and cross-region calls on the hot path
Rough throughput: one web server ~1k-10k QPS, one relational DB ~1k-5k QPS, Redis ~100k QPS per node
Availability nines: 99.9% ≈ 8.8 h downtime/year, 99.99% ≈ 52 min/year, 99.999% ≈ 5 min/year

layout.note: Powers of two and size units
Interview Point: 2-4 questions on latency numbers

chapters.title: API Sketch, Data Model and High-Level Design
points: API sketch: list 3-5 core endpoints with verb, path, params and response, e.g. POST /v1/tweets, GET /v1/feed?cursor=; use cursor pagination and idempotency keys for writes
Choose REST for public CRUD, gRPC for internal low-latency calls, WebSocket/SSE for server push
Data model: list entities, keys and relationships; choose SQL for joins and transactions, NoSQL for scale-out key-value access and flexible schema; justify with access patterns
Index and shard-key choice follows the query pattern; a hot shard key (celebrity user, timestamp) is the classic flaw

High-level design: client → CDN/load balancer → stateless app servers → cache → DB, plus queue for async work and object store for blobs; draw it end to end, then trace one read and one write through it

layout.note: Interview Point: 2-4 questions on API and data model

chapters.title: Deep Dives, Bottlenecks and Common Mistakes
points: Deep dive: pick the 1-2 hardest components (feed fan-out, ID generation, hot keys) and let the interviewer steer; go to mechanism level
Find bottlenecks by walking the diagram: single points of failure, hot partitions, DB write throughput, cache stampede; fix with replication, sharding, caching, queues
State trade-offs explicitly as 'X over Y because Z': consistency vs availability, latency vs cost, fan-out on write vs on read
Mistakes: jumping to the design without requirements, skipping estimates, over-engineering with microservices and Kafka by default, silent while thinking
Mistakes: ignoring failure modes and monitoring, no single clear choice (listing options without deciding), running out of time before deep dives

layout.note: Interview Point: 2-4 questions on bottlenecks and trade-offs

chapters.title: Cheat Sheet: Interview Framework
points: Time split for 45 min: requirements 5, estimates 5, API+data 10, design 10, deep dive 10, wrap-up 5
Formulas: QPS = DAU × actions ÷ 86,400; peak = 2-3× avg; storage = items × size × retention × replicas
Memorize: 2^10/20/30/40 = KB/MB/GB/TB; memory 100 ns, SSD 100 µs, DC hop 0.5 ms, cross-continent 150 ms
Checklist: scope → NFRs → numbers → API → schema → boxes → deep dive → bottlenecks → trade-offs
Always: state assumptions, name the trade-off, trace a request, mention failure and monitoring
